brief: An 8-second explainer: three labelled boxes 'Plan', 'Act', 'Check' appear one at a time in a row, connected by arrows that draw themselves, then an arrow loops from 'Check' back to 'Plan'.
checks: Does the first box that appears contain the word "Plan" spelled correctly and centered inside the box?
Does the second box that appears contain the word "Act" spelled correctly and centered inside the box?
Does the third box that appears contain the word "Check" spelled correctly and centered inside the box?
Do the boxes appear in the order left‑to‑right: Plan, then Act, then Check, with each new box appearing only after the previous one is fully visible?
Does the arrow that connects Plan to Act draw itself smoothly from the Plan box to the Act box, without jumping or skipping?
Does the arrow that connects Act to Check draw itself smoothly from the Act box to the Check box, without jumping or skipping?
Does the looping arrow that goes from the Check box back to the Plan box draw itself smoothly, forming a visible curve or line that completes before the video ends?
Is the text inside each box at least about one‑tenth of the frame height and clearly legible against its background (high contrast)?
Do none of the boxes or arrows touch or cross the outer edge of the frame at any point?
Are the three boxes horizontally aligned on a common baseline and evenly spaced (approximately equal gaps between them)?
Do all movements (appearance of boxes, drawing of arrows) use ease‑in/ease‑out timing rather than a constant linear speed?
Is there some visual change (appearance, movement, color shift) in every second of the video, with no period longer than 0.5 s where nothing moves?
Does the video avoid an empty opening: the first visible element (the Plan box) appears no later than 0.5 s after the start?
Does the final frame hold still for at least 0.5 s before the video ends, with no further animation after the looping arrow is complete?
